params.body:
At launch the Forge site will answer on several hostnames: www.trucks-schoutteet.com, trucks-schoutteet.com, schoutteet.com, www.schoutteet.com and the Forge host. The canonical tag is `url()->current()`, so it names whatever host was visited, and nothing sends a visitor to one host. Each extra domain would be a full copy of the site in Google. Today the bare trucks-schoutteet.com already shows the old site without a redirect.

## What changes

- **`CanonicalHost` middleware**, prepended to every request. With `APP_CANONICAL_HOST` set, any other host gets a 301 to the same path and query on `https://<canonical host>`. The comparison ignores case.
- **`config('app.canonical_host')`** reads `APP_CANONICAL_HOST`. Empty (local, staging before launch): nothing is redirected, so this PR changes nothing until the variable is set.
- **`DEPLOY.md`, "Livegang: domeinen":** the go-live order for the domains. TTL first, Forge domains, basic auth off, DNS (only the A records of `@` and `www`; MX and TXT carry the mail and stay), certificate, environment, Sanity webhook, checks, and the way back.

## Behaviour to know

- Once the variable is set, schoutteet.on-forge.com also redirects to the live host, and so does a POST to `/sanity/webhook` on it. The webhook has to point at the live host (step 7 in `DEPLOY.md`).
- schoutteet.com currently sends visitors to `/en/` on the old site. With this, it keeps the path, so schoutteet.com lands on the Dutch home.
- An old URL on an alias domain takes two hops: alias to canonical host, then the legacy redirect to the new page.

## Checks

- `tests/Feature/CanonicalHostTest.php`: no redirect without the setting; aliases, the bare domain and the Forge host go to the same path and query; the canonical host itself is served.
- `php artisan test`: 61 passed
- `vendor/bin/pint --test`: passed
params.title: Send every other hostname to the canonical host with a 301
